query: What visit reasons point to different departments?

per_column.name: presentation_type
per_column.rationale: Categorizes the visit into presentation types (screening, acute, chronic mgmt, trauma), giving a strong new axis to correlate with department. Sample values are well-grounded readings of the reason text.

per_column.name: acute_vs_chronic
per_column.rationale: Acute/chronic axis is useful for department differentiation, though it partially overlaps conceptually with presentation_type. Values match the source text (twisting injury=acute, MI follow-up=chronic_stable).

per_column.name: primary_system
per_column.rationale: Body-system categorization is highly relevant since departments map closely to systems; provides a clean grouping axis. Values are accurate extractions (knee=musculoskeletal, cough=respiratory, acne=dermatologic).

per_column.name: severity_level
per_column.rationale: Severity adds some leverage but overlaps with the existing urgency column and with acute_vs_chronic. The MI follow-up 'moderate' and stable acne 'moderate' labels are somewhat interpretive but defensible; mostly grounded.

per_column.name: population_context
per_column.rationale: This largely restates the existing age_group column, offering little new analytical leverage for a department-mapping query. Values are well grounded, but redundancy lowers usefulness.

judge.rationale: Most added columns (presentation_type, primary_system, acute_vs_chronic) give genuine new axes strongly relevant to linking visit reasons to departments, and the sampled values are sound readings of the source text with sensible 'not_present' handling. Severity_level is partly redundant with urgency, and population_context largely duplicates the existing age_group, reducing their marginal usefulness, but no hallucinations are observed and groundedness is consistently high.
